29d7:
Arts is a first-year studies option that lets students explore social science and humanities program areas before applying to their program of choice for their second year. All courses that students successfully complete in the Arts program will be credited to the selected Toronto Metropolitan University major. Students can also choose electives from a wide range of areas including marketing, human resources and business – many of which can lead to a minor.

During the UTP Stage II: Arts program students will study courses that introduce them to a wide range of disciplines including psychology, philosophy, politics and environment. Following the completion of Arts - UTP Stage II, including maintaining academic good standing and achieving any program-specific CGPA, students will progress to their chosen major at Toronto Metropolitan University, where they can continue with their Bachelor of Arts program in one of the following areas of study:

  • Environmental and Urban Sustainability
  • Psychology
  • Sociology
  • Philosophy and Politics and Governance

29d9:
International Year One (UTP Stage II): Commerce is equivalent to the first year of Toronto Metropolitan University’s Bachelor of Commerce degree.

Upon the successful completion of International Year One (UTP Stage II), you’ll begin the second year of your degree at TMU, where you’ll have access to industry experts, an optional co-op program, case competitions and networking events to strengthen and put your skills to work in professional environments. Study in the heart of Canada’s business district with faculty committed to ground breaking teaching strategies that combine theory and practice.

6dvo:
TMU, renowned for its career-focused education, provides immersive learning and research experience. Strong industrial network and rigorous academics preparing students for a dynamic career in engineering and science.

Key Program Features:

  • Comprehensive curriculum integrating knowledge with practical applications.
  • Expert faculty dedicated to fostering innovation and critical thinking.
  • Collaborative projects, industry partnership and co-op programs for real-world exposure
  • Access to state-of-the-art laboratories and facilities

TMU’s Faculty of Engineering and Architectural Science’s undergraduate programs prepare students to make meaningful contributions to advancements in technology, health, environmental sustainability, design and more. All engineering programs are accredited by the Canadian Engineering Accreditation Board.
